The Power of Tax Relief + Time

UK pension contributions get tax relief at your marginal rate. For a basic-rate taxpayer, every £80 you put in becomes £100. For a higher-rate taxpayer, every £60 becomes £100. That's a 25% or 67% instant return before any investment growth.

Combined with employer contributions and compound growth over 30+ years, the result is dramatic. Saving £500/month at a 6% real return:

  • For 40 years (age 25-65): £952,000
  • For 30 years (age 35-65): £495,000
  • For 20 years (age 45-65): £225,000
  • For 10 years (age 55-65): £80,000

Starting at 25 instead of 35 nearly doubles your pot — for the same monthly contribution. The first decade of pension saving is the most powerful decade you'll ever have.

Don't Miss the Employer Match

Auto-enrolment mandates a minimum of 8% total contribution (3% employer, 5% employee). Many employers will match additional contributions — common offers include:

  • Match up to 5% (so 5% from you + 5% from them = 10% total)
  • Match £1 for £1 up to a cap (e.g., 6% employer if you contribute 6%)
  • Salary sacrifice arrangements that save NI on both sides

If your employer matches and you're not capturing the full match, you're leaving free money on the table. Even small differences compound enormously — an extra 2% employer match on a £40,000 salary, invested for 30 years at 6%, becomes ~£67,000.

2026 UK Pension Rules

  • Annual allowance: £60,000/year (tapered for high earners)
  • Tax-free lump sum cap: £268,275 (was unlimited pre-2024)
  • Minimum access age: 55 (rising to 57 in April 2028)
  • State Pension age: 66 (rising to 67 between 2026-2028)
  • Carry-forward: Unused allowance from previous 3 years

Frequently Asked Questions

How much should I contribute?
Target 15% of gross income across employer + employee. The auto-enrolment 8% minimum is below what most people need for a comfortable retirement. PLSA estimates ~£43,100/year for a single-person 'comfortable' retirement, implying a pot of ~£600-800k.
2026 annual allowance?
£60,000 standard. Tapered to as low as £10,000 for earners over £260,000. Carry forward unused allowance from previous 3 tax years if needed.
Workplace pension vs SIPP?
Workplace first for the employer match. SIPP next for more control + lower fees. Many people end up with both, plus consolidated old workplace pensions in their SIPP.
When can I access it?
Age 55 (57 from April 2028). 25% tax-free lump sum (capped at £268,275), remainder taxed as income. Early access triggers a ~55% penalty unless on rare medical grounds.
What return rate should I plan for?
6% real (after inflation) is a reasonable baseline for an equity-heavy portfolio. Don't plan around 10%+ — that's optimistic over multi-decade horizons net of fees and inflation.
